evidence: Fixture builds bodies as `body.append(f"\n\nComment {i}: ...")` with no `#### Comments` heading and no `- ` prefix (test lines 122-135).

The test fixture `_realistic_oversized_context` emits no `#### Comments` heading, whereas the real ticket renderer `_format_ticket` does; so `_split_comment_block` finds no comments and returns them all in `head`, making the comment-dropping loop dead code under test even though the fixture claims to be 'shaped like the real 9fd4.'

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make comment grouping robust to bodies that contain `- `-prefixed lines (e.g. group by a stronger comment delimiter than a leading dash).
evidence: `if line.startswith("- ") or not entries:` treats every `- `-prefixed line as a new entry boundary (completion_recovery.py:196).
Docstring: 'Dropping half a comment would be worse than dropping none, so the elision unit is the whole entry' (completion_recovery.py:190-191).

`_format_ticket` emits one `- ` line per comment but a comment body may itself contain lines starting with `- ` (operations.py:69 renders `f"- {(c.get('body') or '').strip()}"`, and the body is arbitrary operator text).
advisory.finding: `_group_comment_entries` starts a new comment entry on any line beginning with `- `, so a single comment whose body contains a markdown bullet is split into multiple 'entries', letting compaction drop half of one comment — the exact outcome the docstring says the whole-entry unit prevents.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid duplicating the exception text — have the remedy point at the already-printed exception rather than re-embedding `str(exc)`.
evidence: `detail = str(exc).strip()` then `... act on its own reported remedy: {detail}` (failure.py:464-469).
`transition_close` builds `f"... could not run ({exc}).{_hint} {_remedy} ..."` where `_remedy = close_gate_remedy(exc, _outcome)` (transition_close.py:342-345).
So the step-budget exception text appears both inside `({exc})` and again inside the remedy sentence.
advisory.finding: For a non-recovery, non-unavailable verifier failure, `close_gate_remedy` embeds `str(exc)` as `detail`, but `transition_close` already interpolates `{exc}` into the same message, so the full (multi-sentence) exception text is printed twice in one CLI error.

evidence: Docstring: 'no single recovery call exceeds the budget' (test lines 165-169).
Assertion filters `if len(r.instructions or "") > _cr._MAX_FINALIZER_INPUT_CHARS` (test line 180), i.e. the 132,000 finalizer bound, not `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` (=40,000).
Per-criterion instructions embed the compacted `ticket_context` (completion_recovery.py:577-582), so the relevant cost cap is the context budget.
advisory.finding: `test_recovery_never_puts_more_than_the_budget_on_the_wire` asserts each recovery request is under `_MAX_FINALIZER_INPUT_CHARS` (132,000), not the per-request context budget `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` (40,000) its docstring claims to pin, so it would not catch a compaction that leaves the on-the-wire context over the declared 40,000 budget.

advisory.finding: The compaction contract's central safety invariant — that acceptance-criteria text is ALWAYS preserved through `compact_recovery_context` — is never asserted. The integration test's fake `_RecoverableRunner.run` derives its verdict from `payload["expected_criteria"]` (sourced from the ticket dict via `explicit_completion_criteria`), not from the compacted `context` string, so the assertions are decoupled from what compaction actually does to the context. A regression where compaction dropped or truncated criteria text from the context would still yield `verdict == "PASS"` and pass every assertion.
scenarios: A future edit to the comment-dropping or description-elision loop accidentally elides a criterion line
`_is_essential` regresses so criterion text is no longer treated as essential

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten `_is_essential` so only true acceptance-criteria/checkbox lines (not arbitrary prose containing a criterion substring) are protected from elision.
evidence: `return any(criterion and criterion in line for criterion in criteria)` (completion_recovery.py:225).
Criteria are short checkbox texts (e.g. `criterion 1`) from `explicit_completion_criteria`; ordinary prose like `... for criterion 1.` contains that substring and is treated as un-elidable.

The final hard-slice fallback (completion_recovery.py:292-295) exists precisely because this phase can fail to reach budget, and its comment calls itself 'Unreachable while the criteria bounds hold' — but over-broad essentiality makes reaching it more likely.
dropped.finding: `_is_essential` uses substring containment `criterion in line`, so any comment or description line that merely mentions a criterion phrase is marked essential and excluded from description-line elision, which can leave the context above budget when much prose references the criteria.
